item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russian sabotage cells damaged a Starlink center in Lithuania and targeted oil facilities in St Petersburg, while anti-Putin groups operated inside Russia. President Trump signed an executive order waiving a new Russia sanctions package, prompting Zelenskyy to accuse him of rewarding Putin. Russian missiles and drones struck Ukrainian infrastructure, killing one person and injuring eight in Kyiv, and a drone strike on a park in Kharkiv Oblast killed children and an infant. Ukraine used drones to evacuate an injured soldier and to airlift a wounded soldier, a first-of-its-kind operation, and 75,767 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli police have arrested ten suspects after settlers attacked a US photographer, a French mayor and other civilians in the West Bank, torching cars and olive trees and wounding farmers. In Gaza the World Food Programme is ending aid for half a million people because of funding shortfalls, while UNICEF reports that 340 children have been killed despite a ceasefire. The conflict continues to generate high mortality, with 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran has installed a new defence minister and intensified IRGC drone and artillery strikes in Iraqi Kurdistan while launching missiles near the UAE and bombarding a tug in the Strait of Hormuz, expanding its maritime campaign. An explosion struck an Iranian-backed group in Iraq and Tehran urged the reopening of the strait. A powerful African military is considering joining Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey to defend Saudi interests against Houthi attacks. The US ambassador to Israel condemned a settler attack on a US journalist in the West Bank. 123 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
Houthis have launched a ballistic missile strike on a Saudi-backed Yemeni army training camp in Shabwa, killing more than 50 soldiers. The attack follows a pattern of recent Houthi missile and ballistic strikes against Yemeni government forces. Iran is reported to be providing targeting and intelligence support to the Houthis, while Egypt has pledged support to Saudi Arabia against them. The war produced 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
Syrian authorities report a suspect in the Baniyas mass killings was arrested, while a Syrian soldier was killed by unidentified gunmen in eastern Deir ez-Zor. Damascus warns the Israeli Defense Forces over its continued buffer-zone enforcement in southern Syria, and the governor of Sweida says the capital remains open to dialogue despite security concerns. Jordan’s king reaffirmed support for Syria’s sovereignty, and the Syrian Kurdish community is reported to prefer Bashar al-Assad over Erdogan. 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
US troops have completed their withdrawal, leaving Iraq to confront new security and governance challenges while Gulf states rank higher in disaster resilience than Iraq. Baghdad and Tehran are deepening security cooperation and have activated joint committees, even as Iran’s envoy warned that border security is a red line and Iranian forces attacked the Komala Kurdish opposition group. Iraqi authorities are pursuing legal action against media incitement supporting pro-Iran armed groups, arresting a lawyer who brandished a gun in court and urging prosecutions, while the YBŞ is negotiating integration into state security institutions. Nineveh continues heritage reconstruction and the Jordanian king has invited the Iraqi president for regional de-escalation talks. The conflict recorded 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The Sudanese army has used drones to strike a livestock market, killing civilians, and also hit a site in West Kordofan that killed four civilians. RSF drones have attacked an artisanal gold mine in South Kordofan and a gold-mining area on the Egypt border, causing civilian casualties. A drone attack near a market in Khartoum killed dozens, while another near a southern Sudan market killed scores. These incidents show a widening of drone use against civilian economic sites, beyond the earlier focus on combatants. 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Ethiopian forces have installed an interim administration in Tigray and are advancing toward the Eritrean border, while a pro-government militia says it has seized the regional airport and reports Eritrean forces suffered losses there. The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging both Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate the fighting. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP. This adds the militia’s capture of the airport, reported Eritrean casualties, and the involvement of Secretary Rubio, which were not mentioned in the prior briefing.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Fitgharan forces now control the Mogadishu-Baidoa corridor while Laftagareen forces have taken Buurhakaba and another town in the Bay region, intensifying fighting in southern Somalia. Al Shabaab detonated an IED in Mandera, injuring six civilians, and the ICRC treated 148 wounded after heavy combat in Baidoa. Ethiopia announced the withdrawal of more than 3,000 troops from Somalia as its own conflict escalates, and Somaliland and Puntland were designated as "friendly" in an Israeli security framework. Somalia is screening travelers after Kenya confirmed an imported Ebola case and has agreed to acquire Pakistani JF‑17 fighter jets. The UCDP recorded 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:
Malian forces and their Russian allies are conducting indiscriminate drone strikes that have killed 94 civilians, while both the Malian army and rebel groups are committing abuses against civilians. In Nigeria, terrorists killed soldiers at a Borno military post and a convoy attack in Borno resulted in the loss of 15 soldiers and task force members. Burkina Faso, Niger and Mali have resumed talks with ECOWAS after a withdrawal, indicating diplomatic engagement alongside the violence. The conflict remains deadly, with 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:
Bandits are raiding villages and blocking a deputy governor convoy in Zamfara while gunmen shot the Miyetti Allah chairman in Plateau and assaulted police stations in Plateau, Abia and Borno, killing several officers. ISWAP militants placed landmines on a highway in Borno that killed eight soldiers and later claimed an attack that killed 21 soldiers and militiamen at an army base. President Tinubu approved security equipment to protect trains from bandit attacks and an air traffic controller remains captive after being abducted at Sokoto airport for 52 days. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

In Ituri, suspected ADF rebels killed 77 civilians. The coalition’s actions have intensified fighting in the eastern provinces. item.description:

Pakistan suspended trade at two Iran border crossings, citing security and smuggling concerns, while trade with Afghanistan fell sharply after border closures. The conflict recorded 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP. These actions intensify cross-border violence and economic pressure beyond the school roof collapse previously reported.

item.title: The Philippines: the situation
item.description:
The Philippines summoned China’s ambassador after a Chinese official warned that China could easily win a war, prompting lawmakers to call for a review of water-cannon use against Chinese vessels. Vice Admiral Rommel Supangan assumed command of the Philippine Coast Coast Guard, which rescued four people, including a child, on Hagonoy Island in Surigao del Sur. Chinese coast guard and navy ships entered waters near the Pratas Islands and Scarborough Shoal, while Taiwan’s coast guard and maritime forces repelled 16 mainland vessels in a coordinated operation. The United States and the Philippines held their 16th bilateral maritime exercise in the West Philippine Sea, and the PCG conducted an anti-piracy drill with Japan, and there were 176 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

A Chinese suspect was detained in Bangkok after attempting a 100,000 baht border crossing, and Malaysia appointed a new facilitator for southern Thailand peace talks. Cambodia and Thailand agreed on confidence-building measures at a UNCLOS meeting, and the WTO and multilateral partners reviewed progress on a supply chain finance initiative. Floods in Thailand killed 80 people as waters receded. The conflict recorded 35 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Colombia: the situation
item.description:
Rescue operations continue after an earthquake left more than 224 dead, while protests over the removal of artworks from the National Museum have led to water-cannon use on demonstrators in Bogotá. The president is preparing to sign a decree defining maritime boundaries for the San Andres, Providencia and Santa Catalina Archipelago, and former rebel leaders have been charged with war crimes against Indigenous groups. An evangelist pastor was murdered by gang members he had evangelized, a Colombian chef was killed in a crash in Attard, and a priest died when a cross fell during a livestreamed mass. ICE agents tackled a Colombian asylum seeker in Washington, and the Mobile Anti-Riot Squad (ESMAD) has returned to operate in the country. The conflict recorded 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

European and Ecuadorian police cooperation produced 20 arrests in a major drug-trafficking bust and nightly curfews were imposed across Ecuador from November 1 to 10 under a state of emergency. item.description:

item.title: Haiti's gang war: the situation

Sri Lankan police STF and army contingents have been deployed to Haiti, joining a Bangladesh advance team for the UN security mission, and 500 Sri Lankan soldiers were sent to reinforce the GSF. The United Nations renewed sanctions on Haiti and allocated US$75 million for life-saving aid to 507,000 people. A secret arms deal links Haitian police to Dolly Parton’s nephew, a former lawmaker, with millions missing. 193 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
